hero.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
hero.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
hero.body:
Concerns over contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks are prompting South Florida residents to reconsider their food choices, with some avoiding leafy greens entirely. The outbreaks have affected thousands nationwide and include lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials have confirmed local cases stretching from the Palm Beaches to the Treasure Coast, including two cases in St. Lucie County.

 The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May. Two cases were reported in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The contamination concerns have led families across the region to change their eating habits at restaurants, grocery stores, and fast-food chains.

 Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, who were visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Other families are similarly steering clear of leafy greens altogether as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country. The widespread nature of the outbreaks has left many consumers uncertain about which products are safe to purchase and consume.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, offered guidance for consumers looking to maintain healthy diets while avoiding potentially contaminated produce. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She advises consumers to focus on produce with protective outer layers and to wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them.

 For those seeking alternatives to leafy greens, Barone suggests that beans and nuts are safe options that still provide fiber and protein. She specifically recommends cleaning produce using a mixture of one part distilled white vinegar to three parts water. The outbreaks have highlighted the importance of proper food handling and preparation practices for consumers across South Florida.

cards.headline: Two men killed in early morning shooting on Southeast Rivergreen Circle in Port St. Lucie
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is investigating a double fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in a residential neighborhood. Officers responded around 3:30 a.m. to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots. When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries. Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22.

Preliminary investigators believe some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence over a residential key and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved. The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information.

Neighbors described a chaotic scene in the early morning hours. John Adams was awake working in his garage when he heard the violence unfold. "I was just working on my bicycle and I heard gunshots. Maybe two, three and I stayed in the garage and then I heard a girl screaming," said Adams. He described the massive emergency response that followed. "Every police officer in Port St. Lucie was here, there was twenty squads, two ambulances, two firetrucks, a helicopter. It was just mayhem," Adams said. A police officer told him they photographed 16 casings at the scene. "Just devastating, terrible. My heart goes out to them," said Adams. Another neighbor who did not want to be identified told WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache that she dialed 911 and stayed with one of the wounded men until help arrived.

Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public. All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: Snyder Drives in Five as St. Lucie Mets Hold Off Cardinals, 8-6
cards.teaser:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder
cards.body:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder went 4-for-5 with a home run, triple and five RBIs, helping St. Lucie win the three-game series two games to one.

After allowing the Cardinals to score first in each of the opening two games, the Mets took control with three runs in the first inning.

Randy Guzman opened the scoring with a 107 mph ground ball that Palm Beach third baseman Jonathan Mejia stopped but could not make a throw on, allowing Marco Vargas to score. Snyder followed with a two-run single that gave the Mets a 3-0 lead.

Starting pitcher Ethan Lanthier worked through early traffic and completed 2 1/3 scoreless innings. He allowed one hit and struck out four.

Tyler McLoughlin followed with 1 2/3 scoreless innings and earned the victory, improving his record to 2-2. McLoughlin has allowed only one earned run over his last 12 appearances and has now recorded six consecutive scoreless outings.

St. Lucie added three more runs in the third inning when Snyder launched his second home run of the season. The three-run shot brought home Mike Tauchman and Guzman and extended the Mets' advantage to 6-0.

Snyder continued his strong afternoon with a triple in the seventh inning. Branny De Oleo then hit his seventh home run of the season, a two-run shot that pushed St. Lucie's lead to 8-1.

Palm Beach made the game interesting in the bottom of the seventh.

Yairo Padilla hit his first home run of the season, a grand slam against Ernesto Mercedes, as the Cardinals scored five runs in the inning and cut the Mets' lead to 8-6.

Palm Beach brought the potential tying run to the plate in the ninth after Trevor Haskins was hit by a pitch. Miguel Mejias responded by striking out the next three batters to finish the game and earn his third save of the season.

St. Lucie pitchers combined for 17 strikeouts, marking the third consecutive game in which the Mets recorded double-digit strikeouts.

The Mets improved to 8-14 in the second half and 41-47 overall. Palm Beach fell to 13-10 in the second half and 65-43 overall.

St. Lucie will have an off day Monday before opening a new series against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Tuesday. First pitch is scheduled for 6:05 p.m.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September, citing low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said.

Dambeck said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on passenger demand. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said.

The airline's Boston route from Vero Beach is performing well in contrast to the struggling JFK service. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route potentially returning in the future, as the airline will evaluate continuously. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offering free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.

 The program offers one alarm per household and has no income or priority group requirements, making it available to any qualifying resident regardless of financial status. The alarms are available while supplies last on a first-come, first-served basis, so interested residents should act promptly to secure one. Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out an online survey to determine their eligibility for the program. For more information about the free pool alarm program, residents can call (772) 462-3501.

 According to the coalition, a pool alarm serves as one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning. The program emphasizes that pool alarms are not a standalone safety solution but rather part of a comprehensive approach to water safety. Residents should note that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm, but the battery is not included with the free alarm.

 The initiative aims to increase water safety awareness and provide practical tools to help prevent drowning incidents in residential pools throughout Martin County. By distributing these alarms at no cost, the program seeks to remove financial barriers that might otherwise prevent families from implementing additional safety measures around their pools. The combination of free access and the comprehensive safety messaging demonstrates the coalition's commitment to protecting children and preventing water-related accidents in the community.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project
cards.body:
Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized.

 The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

 Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said the school was already scheduled for significant construction before the hurricane struck. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Gernaine.

 "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on." The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach firefighters rescue dog from raw sewage lift station
cards.teaser: A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue.
cards.body:
A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue by Boynton Beach Fire Rescue Department. Squad 6 crews arrived and assessed the scene before upgrading the incident to a Special Operations confined space rescue, the department said. Firefighters developed a rescue plan and had Firefighter Ramirez properly rigged and ready to enter the lift station.

 From the time he went on air, Firefighter Ramirez rescued the dog and safely exited the lift station in just 4 minutes, the department said. Once above ground, crews decontaminated the dog and gave it oxygen before turning it over to Animal Control. Animal Control successfully reunited the dog with its owner, according to a Facebook post from the department.

cards.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian as severe weather strikes Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather battered the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to th
cards.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather battered the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom captured the waterspout moving through the area.

 The severe weather stretched across the region, bringing heavy rain and significant lightning activity. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotters recorded video of heavy rain moving through the area.

 Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said.

 Lightning strikes caused fires in Port St. Lucie. Lucie County Fire District crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot.

 Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening. Radar picked up significant lightning in the area at the time, though Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

 The severe weather extended to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Moore O'Rourke summarized what many across the region felt as the storms moved through. "I mean it was radical.

 I mean it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather reminded residents of nature's unpredictable power.

cards.headline: Wellington teen injured after electric bike rider strikes him during stunt near Lion Country Safari
cards.teaser: A Wellington teenager suffered multiple injuries, including broken bones, after being struck by an electric bike rider performing a wheelie on Tuesday night.
cards.body:
Seventeen-year-old Chad Filer said he was riding his scooter along a relatively isolated stretch of road between the Deer Run community and Lion Country Safari on Tuesday night when three teenage boys on dirt and electric bikes approached him. According to Chad, one rider began performing a wheelie and intentionally swerved toward him in what he described as a common "bike life" stunt meant to intimidate people before pulling away at the last second, but instead the bike struck the right side of his body.

 Chad estimates the rider was traveling around 40 mph when the impact sent him to the ground. A driver stopped to help, and Chad said the riders initially stayed nearby and told him he was "fine," but once witnesses called 911, the group fled.

 Doctors found Chad suffered broken metatarsal bones, three broken toes, significant bruising and multiple road rash injuries across his chest, knee, elbow and side. His mother, Cortez Hornsby, said part of one nipple was partially detached in the crash. The family faces mounting medical expenses because Chad's health insurance through work was not scheduled to begin until next month.

 Hornsby says she called the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office and was told this is a county-wide problem. She also says deputies told her that based on how isolated the crash site is and the lack of cameras, it may be difficult to find the teens. Chad cannot work while he heals, and the scooter he relied on for transportation was heavily damaged.

cards.headline: Wildfire burns 2,500 acres in western Palm Beach County, 30% contained
cards.teaser: A wildfire burning in western Palm Beach County has grown to 2,500 acres and is 30% contained, according to the Florida Forest Service.
cards.body:
A wildfire burning in western Palm Beach County has grown to 2,500 acres and is 30% contained, according to the Florida Forest Service. The Berger Fire remains active in Palm Beach County within the Florida Forest Service's Everglades field unit. As of 3:02 p.m. Saturday, the Florida Forest Service reported the fire had burned approximately 2,500 acres.

 The wildfire comes as the region experienced severe weather Friday that left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Residents sent multiple videos to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showing a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area, with one resident reporting her rain gauge caught over 3 inches.

 The severe weather stretched all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Port St. Lucie also saw significant lightning activity.

 The St. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Fire crews also responded to an evening house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue.

 While radar picked up significant lightning in the area at the time, the St. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

 Merry Moore O'Rourke, a resident who experienced the storms in Port St. Lucie, described the intensity of the weather. "All of a sudden, it got black.

 The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said. She summed up what many across the region felt as the storms moved through. "I mean it was radical.

 I mean it was it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather served as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. The Berger Fire situation remains developing as officials continue containment efforts.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrests nephew in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes
cards.teaser: Dale A. Mincey, 41, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with the death of his uncle, 66-year-old Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes.
cards.body:
Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with Barnes' death. Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. Deputies said the fatal shooting was premeditated.

 Karen Moye, who lived in the home with Mincey and Barnes, was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police, an arrest affidavit said. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said during a press conference Tuesday that detectives uncovered information indicating Moye, the victim's sister and mother of the suspect, knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to the homicide investigation. She has been charged with false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. He leaves behind three adult children.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County man leads Martin County deputies on 100 mph chase through Indiantown
cards.teaser: Markell Tillman, 33, drove more than 100 mph on State Road 710 before leading deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown and onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City.
cards.body:
A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710, one of the area's most dangerous roads. Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled. Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly.

 Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95. Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody.

 Tillman was arrested on charges including fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement with 1,162 stops in four weeks
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies to target speeding and reckless driving on Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break. He is also placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern. Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said the county sees a lot of excessive speeding, noting that someone recently passed her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues described stopping a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, his top recorded speed was 73 mph.

 In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

 The severe weather stretched to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Moore O'Rourke described the experience as frightening. "All of a sudden, it got black.

 The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," she said. "I mean it was radical. I mean it was a little scary."

 Friday's severe weather left a trail of impacts from Sebastian through Port St. Lucie and into Palm Beach and Okeechobee counties, serving as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power.

cards.headline: House fire reported on Bellevue Avenue during Port St. Lucie storms
cards.teaser: Fire crews responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during Friday's severe weather, with the fire marshal's office still investigating the cause.
cards.body:
Lucie County Fire District responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue in Port St. Lucie on Friday evening during severe weather. At the time of the storm, radar picked up a significant amount of lightning in the area. The district said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

 The fire occurred as Port St. Lucie experienced heavy rain and lightning activity. WPTV weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area, and Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches.

 Earlier, Lucie County Fire District crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Moore O'Rourke described the conditions, saying the sky got black, the wind started raging, and the sky had lit up like she had not seen. She called the storms radical and a little scary.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September, citing low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said.

Dambeck said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on passenger demand. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said.

The airline's Boston route from Vero Beach is performing well in contrast to the struggling JFK service. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route potentially returning in the future, as the airline will evaluate continuously. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.
