cards.headline: Fort Pierce neighbors pack planning meeting over Causeway Cove high-rise development proposal
cards.teaser: The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall.
cards.body:
The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space.

 The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing.

 Neighbors packed the chamber during the Monday meeting. Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic, saying nobody has thought this out and predicting massive traffic jams with nobody able to get on or off the island.

 City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved, stating the city does not have a play here and this is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step in the process.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie couple fights rezoning of lot behind home near Crosstown Parkway
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie couple is searching for answers after the city council voted to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial.
cards.body:
Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo have called Port St. Lucie home since purchasing their property, drawn by what Margaret described as the beautiful setting and backyard views of nature. In a unanimous vote, the Port St.

 Lucie City Council approved rezoning the lot behind their yard, where trees currently stand, from residential to commercial. One council member said the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood, explaining that adding commercial closer to neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, which reduces overall traffic because shorter trips reduce the burden on the overall network.

 The Mucciolos fought the rezoning for months and feel their voices have gone unheard. The council held its second reading Monday. While there was public comment, it was what is called a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges, applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion.

 The Mucciolos say the process needs to change to be logical, transparent, caring, and provide hope for people. They say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one. Joseph Mucciolo said he believes in six months or a year, the trees behind their home will be gone.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: Dave and Faren Motz of Hobe Sound are asking for community support as Dave battles head and neck cancer, facing nearly $20,000 in out-of-pocket costs for treatment.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis. Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren homeschooled all three of their children, and the family started a farm where they served children. Years later, the couple moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer.

 As the couple searched for healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource. Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket.

 Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid. Dave, a former firefighter who had long been the family's provider, now has an 85% chance of recovery according to doctors. Faren now works to support them both at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show support can visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents return home after nearly 2 years following structural damage repairs
cards.teaser: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos.
cards.body:
Residents told WPTV they were notified last month they could return to their condos, after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. Katie Johnson was the first to share to WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return.

 WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, saying they're still moving the dirt back under the buildings.

 Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot. Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia.

 Eric Johnson said the financial toll has been severe and that he and his family had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors, like Eric Johnson, who cannot return and feels so bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Residents Report Five Cyclospora Cases Since May
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health has confirmed five cases of cyclospora in the Treasure Coast region since May amid nationwide produce contamination outbreaks.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County. The cases are part of nationwide outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora linked to contaminated produce, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, causing many South Florida residents to change their eating habits and avoid leafy greens altogether.

 Families across the region are steering clear of salads and contaminated produce that can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are avoiding lettuce and similar foods. Jenny Rhodes said she misses her salads and berries but believes it is better to be careful.

 In West Palm Beach, George Lorenz said he has heard about the outbreak and is staying away from affected produce. In Boynton Beach, shopper Hendriette Peckens said she bought oranges, apples and bread instead of greens and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

 Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said the outbreaks are not an excuse to abandon healthy eating. She recommended consumers focus on produce with protective outer layers, suggesting they stick to melon and foods with harder skin that can be peeled, including bananas, melons and avocados. However, she warned that people still need to wash these items before cutting into them and peeling them. Barone also said beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein.

 Barone's biggest warning was to avoid bagged lettuce if possible. She recommended buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. She also warned that berries, especially raspberries, are difficult to clean properly and should be avoided.

 Barone recommended cleaning produce using a 1 to 3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water. Consumers should soak, massage and clean off produce and make sure to cook vegetables. She emphasized that washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them is essential, and consumers should wash items with harder skins before cutting into them.

hero.headline: Snyder Drives in Five as St. Lucie Mets Hold Off Cardinals, 8-6
hero.teaser:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder
hero.body:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder went 4-for-5 with a home run, triple and five RBIs, helping St. Lucie win the three-game series two games to one.

After allowing the Cardinals to score first in each of the opening two games, the Mets took control with three runs in the first inning.

Randy Guzman opened the scoring with a 107 mph ground ball that Palm Beach third baseman Jonathan Mejia stopped but could not make a throw on, allowing Marco Vargas to score. Snyder followed with a two-run single that gave the Mets a 3-0 lead.

Starting pitcher Ethan Lanthier worked through early traffic and completed 2 1/3 scoreless innings. He allowed one hit and struck out four.

Tyler McLoughlin followed with 1 2/3 scoreless innings and earned the victory, improving his record to 2-2. McLoughlin has allowed only one earned run over his last 12 appearances and has now recorded six consecutive scoreless outings.

St. Lucie added three more runs in the third inning when Snyder launched his second home run of the season. The three-run shot brought home Mike Tauchman and Guzman and extended the Mets' advantage to 6-0.

Snyder continued his strong afternoon with a triple in the seventh inning. Branny De Oleo then hit his seventh home run of the season, a two-run shot that pushed St. Lucie's lead to 8-1.

Palm Beach made the game interesting in the bottom of the seventh.

Yairo Padilla hit his first home run of the season, a grand slam against Ernesto Mercedes, as the Cardinals scored five runs in the inning and cut the Mets' lead to 8-6.

Palm Beach brought the potential tying run to the plate in the ninth after Trevor Haskins was hit by a pitch. Miguel Mejias responded by striking out the next three batters to finish the game and earn his third save of the season.

St. Lucie pitchers combined for 17 strikeouts, marking the third consecutive game in which the Mets recorded double-digit strikeouts.

The Mets improved to 8-14 in the second half and 41-47 overall. Palm Beach fell to 13-10 in the second half and 65-43 overall.

St. Lucie will have an off day Monday before opening a new series against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Tuesday. First pitch is scheduled for 6:05 p.m.

cards.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
cards.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate.

 Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

 Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation.

 The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

cards.headline: President Trump to Attend World Cup Final in New Jersey with Stepped-Up Security
cards.teaser: The World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey has been designated a Level 1 Special Event with President Trump attending the trophy presentation and enhanced security from multiple federal agencies.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup began with 48 teams playing over 39 days. Now it comes down to one final match Sunday in New Jersey. As Argentina and Spain prepare to take the pitch, a sprawling network of federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies continue with a game plan two years in the making to ensure the final is safe.

 A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament.

 The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

 The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle.

cards.headline: Major League Baseball Restricts iPad Use in Dugouts to Block AI Decision-Making
cards.teaser: MLB has made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence to make in-game decisions about substitutions and pitch calling.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started.

 MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches. The memo was first reported by The Athletic and was obtained by The Associated Press.

 A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks mile world record with 3:42.66 run in London
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr shattered a 27-year-old world record on Saturday, running the mile in 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event in London.
cards.body:
Great Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 on Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. The 27-year-old made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at Saturday's Diamond League event in London. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial.

 His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

 Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles. He also set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events.

cards.headline: Spain defeats Argentina 1-0 to win 2026 World Cup in extra time thriller
cards.teaser: Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute of extra time, burying a left-footed s
cards.body:
Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute of extra time, burying a left-footed shot just under the crossbar after pouncing on a bouncing ball in the box. It is Spain's second World Cup championship and first since 2010.

 Spain was absolutely dominant throughout the match in terms of possession and shot attempts. The team took 15 shots in regulation while Argentina managed none. Spain also won nine corners compared to Argentina's single corner kick.

 Despite this overwhelming advantage, Lionel Messi and Argentina found a way to hang on and force the match into extra time. Torres broke through in the opening moment of the second 15-minute period of extra time to finally secure the victory for Spain.

 Argentina's task became even more difficult when Enzo Fernandez was sent off in second-half stoppage time after receiving his second yellow card. Fernandez was carded for a reckless play that sent Spain defender Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air, forcing Argentina to finish the match with only 10 players. About two minutes after play resumed, another foul gave Lamine Yamal a chance to seal the victory from about 22 yards out on a free kick.

 His curling strike toward the right post was saved by Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, who made a diving stop for his 10th save of the afternoon, the most ever recorded in a World Cup final. Martinez leaped to his feet afterward, punching the air and encouraging the crowd to get loud before the match eventually went to extra time.

 With the victory, Spain became the first nation to simultaneously hold the World Cup crowns in both men's and women's soccer. The final was the 104th and last match of the expanded 48-team tournament played across the United States, Canada and Mexico. Because there were more matches than any previous World Cup, the tournament produced 308 total goals, more than any other edition in history. According to FIFA, the 2026 World Cup was officially the most attended ever.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts earn top 15 national finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.teaser: Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Sk
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine represented the gym at the national competition and will advance to compete at the higher level. The trio each discovered gymnastics through unique experiences, with Rose-Daris crediting her ability to do a cartwheel, Supan finding inspiration from watching gymnasts on YouTube, and Rine enjoying the opportunity to continuously learn new skills.

 Head Coach Candice Lazuka praised the team's performance throughout the season, noting they competed at local meets before advancing through states and regionals to reach nationals. At the AAU Nationals competition in Knoxville, the team delivered an exceptional performance that nearly achieved a perfect score. Lazuka explained that earning a perfect 10 is extremely difficult, but the gymnasts managed to score a 9.9, coming very close to perfection. The strong showing at nationals secured their qualification for the Junior Olympics.

 The three gymnasts expressed excitement about the upcoming opportunity to compete at the Junior Olympics in Iowa. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described her feelings about the achievement, saying it's happy and exciting at the same time. The young athletes are preparing to take on competitors from across the country at the prestigious event.

 Looking ahead to the Junior Olympics competition, the gymnasts are setting their goals and focusing on specific events. When asked what she is focused on heading into the Junior Olympics, Rine said getting first place on floors. The qualification represents a significant achievement for both the individual gymnasts and Flip City Gym and Cheer as a whole.

 The team's progression from local competitions through the state and regional levels to nationals, and now to the Junior Olympics, demonstrates the dedication and skill development that Lazuka has cultivated in her athletes. The upcoming competition in Iowa will provide Rose-Daris, Supan, and Rine the chance to test themselves against the nation's top junior gymnasts.

hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. Led by Summer Faerman, the program connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

 The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

 Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

 As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to children at 35 summer sites
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program while school is out.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program, according to Food Bank leaders. The nonprofit organization supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County while school is out for the summer. During a live Shining A Light broadcast on WPTV, CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county.

 The organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, hunger doesn't take a summer break, highlighting the need for continued support during the summer months. The Summer BreakSpot program provides free meals to children and teens 18 and younger during the summer when school cafeterias are closed. Food Bank leaders said the meals are distributed through partner locations across Palm Beach County to help families facing food insecurity during the summer. Kendall said the Food Bank's partnership with Summer BreakSpot helps ensure children continue receiving nutritious meals while school is out.

 During the broadcast, viewers got a close look at the large-scale kitchen operation responsible for preparing meals daily. Chef Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks. The loading dock operation featured drivers and volunteers preparing for morning deliveries to Summer BreakSpot sites throughout Palm Beach County. The Palm Beach County Food Bank said volunteers and community support are critical to maintaining the program during the busy summer season.

 The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach. Food Bank leaders said the organization continues seeking volunteers, donations and community partnerships to support its mission of reducing childhood hunger in Palm Beach County. Families looking for Summer BreakSpot meal locations can find participating sites throughout the county during the summer months.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free promotion through August 10
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo has extended its popular Kids Free promotion and announced the return of adults-only Wild Night Out events.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Zoo has extended its Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, according to Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, who shared updates during WPTV's "Shining A Light" segment from the zoo Monday morning. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Joiner said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission. Zoo officials emphasized that families still receive the full zoo experience through the promotion, including access to exhibits, shaded walkways and animal encounters. The zoo is also encouraging visitors to stay cool with indoor spaces, shaded pathways and frozen treats available throughout the park.

 The zoo announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include Paws & Santa Claus in July, Tails & Touchdowns in August and Decades After Dark in September. The events will feature live entertainment, themed activities and performances from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback. July's event will also serve as an early preview of this year's Zoo Lights celebration, with new lighting displays, updated activations and a noticeably different experience compared to previous years. The zoo's newest koala joey is officially a boy and has been named Bonza, which Joiner said is Australian slang for awesome or excellent.

cards.headline: Downtown Delray Beach launches Wellness Pass with free fitness classes and spa deals for July and August
cards.teaser: The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August. The mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses.
cards.body:
Downtown Delray Beach is encouraging residents and visitors to prioritize health and self-care this summer through a new Wellness Pass featuring free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness-focused offers across the city's downtown district. The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August.

 According to the DDA, the mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses throughout Downtown Delray Beach. The pass does not require an app download. Miller Physical Therapy is also participating with wellness-related services and promotions. The program arrives as wellness tourism and fitness-focused experiences continue to grow in popularity across South Florida. Many consumers are seeking affordable ways to stay active, reduce stress and support local businesses during the summer months.

cards.headline: Delray Beach dance studio hosts Bridgerton masquerade gala July 24 for ninth anniversary
cards.teaser: Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach is celebrating nine years with a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala featuring themed decor and dancing.
cards.body:
Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, located at 247 SE Sixth Ave., is hosting a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala on July 24 to celebrate its ninth anniversary. The studio is owned by world champion dancers Mar Martinez and Clifton Sepulveda and has built a reputation for welcoming dancers of all experience levels, from beginners to competitive performers. The anniversary gala will feature themed décor, dancing and a celebration of the studio's growth over the past nine years.

 The studio is launching a Summer Boot Camp series beginning July 18 and continuing every Saturday through August. According to Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, the classes are designed to help participants learn ballroom and Latin dance fundamentals in a fun, supportive environment. Another upcoming event is a DJ Latin Dance Night open to the public on July 31 from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Martinez and Sepulveda are also preparing to teach a dance class at Florida Atlantic University beginning in August. More information about upcoming events and classes is available at FredAstaireDelrayBeach.com.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free program through August 10
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo extended its Kids Free promotion through August 10, allowing up to four children ages 3 to 12 to receive free admission with one adult ticket.
cards.body:
Palm Beach Zoo extended its popular Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, according to zoo officials. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, shared the updates during WPTV's "Shining A Light" segment from the zoo Monday morning. Joiner said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission. Zoo officials emphasized that families still receive the full zoo experience through the promotion, including access to exhibits, shaded walkways and animal encounters. The zoo is also encouraging visitors to stay cool with indoor spaces, shaded pathways and frozen treats available throughout the park.

 The zoo's newest koala joey is officially a boy and now has a name: Bonza. Joiner said that's Aussie slang for "awesome" or "excellent" during the interview. Palm Beach Zoo also announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include "Paws & Santa Claus" in July, "Tails & Touchdowns" in August and "Decades After Dark" in September. The events will feature live entertainment, themed activities and performances from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback. Palm Beach Zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

hero.headline: Florida Falls Outside Top Five Most Retirement-Friendly States in New National Ranking
hero.teaser: Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a
hero.body:
Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a premier retirement destination. The assessment from Moneywise evaluated states based on factors affecting retirees' quality of life and financial security. The ranking represents a shift in how retirement destinations are evaluated across the United States, excluding a state that has traditionally dominated conversations about ideal places to spend retirement years.

 Florida has traditionally marketed itself as an ideal location for retirees, with its warm climate and lack of state income tax serving as major draws for older Americans. The state's senior population has grown substantially over decades, with retirees from northeastern and midwestern states relocating to Florida communities in significant numbers. However, the new analysis considered multiple factors that affect retirement living, including cost of living, healthcare access, tax structures, and overall quality of life indicators. The exclusion of Florida from the top five suggests that other locations now offer more attractive combinations of affordability and amenities for retirees.

 Florida has faced rising property insurance costs, increased housing prices, and higher overall living expenses in recent years, factors that may have influenced its position in the ranking. These economic pressures have created new challenges for retirees on fixed incomes who must balance the appeal of warm weather and outdoor lifestyles against escalating costs of maintaining their standard of living.

 Despite these financial headwinds, the findings arrive as Florida continues to see substantial population growth, with many new residents arriving at or near retirement age. The state's economy remains heavily dependent on retiree spending and the industries that support senior populations, including healthcare, real estate, and leisure services.

 How this ranking affects future retirement migration patterns to Florida remains uncertain, though the state's established retirement communities and infrastructure continue to attract older Americans seeking warmer climates and outdoor lifestyles. The ranking signals that retirees now have compelling alternatives to consider when choosing their retirement destinations, potentially reshaping demographic trends that have favored Florida for generations. While the specific states that ranked in the top five were not detailed in the available information, Florida's absence from the list marks a notable development for a state whose identity and economy have been closely tied to its status as a retirement haven.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds, David Jolly Lead Florida Governor's Race as Primary Nears
cards.teaser: Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly hold commanding positions in Florida's governor's race with the August 18 primary approaching. A Tyson Group survey rele
cards.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly hold commanding positions in Florida's governor's race with the August 18 primary approaching.

 A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48% among Republicans, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8%, and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%.

 About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has raised more than $90 million across his campaign operation and received President Donald Trump's endorsement.

 The Republican primary has grown increasingly contentious as Collins, who was appointed lieutenant governor by Gov. Ron DeSantis in August 2025, attempts to consolidate support despite not receiving DeSantis's endorsement. During a Thursday campaign call, Collins positioned himself as the strongest alternative to Donalds and urged Renner to leave the race, saying the primary is between Donalds and himself.

 Meanwhile, Fishback faces challenges on multiple fronts. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen.

 Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments.

 Collins is also challenging whether Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing on the residency question is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. The residency challenge adds another complication to Fishback's campaign as he attempts to gain traction in a race where Donalds maintains a significant polling advantage over the rest of the Republican field.

 On the Democratic side, Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit managing trust funds for people with disabilities, with the alleged scheme operating from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, and Govoni served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S.

 Senate campaign. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. The connection nonetheless presents a challenge for Jolly as he seeks to maintain his lead in the Democratic primary while managing questions about his past associations with individuals now facing serious federal charges.

cards.headline: Florida Republican Gubernatorial Candidate Faces Antisemitism Ad and Residency Challenge
cards.teaser: Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback faces a $400,000 attack ad and a court hearing over whether he meets the state's seven-year residency requirement for governors.
cards.body:
Businessman James Fishback is facing pressure on two fronts in Florida's Republican gubernatorial primary. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen.

 Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign.

 Lt. Gov. Jay Collins is challenging Fishback's candidacy, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors.

 A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. Because ballots have already been printed, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Fishback at 8% in the Republican primary.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance Lowers Homeowners Rates by Average 5.6% in Florida
cards.teaser: Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings the company is required to pass along to customers have been passed along.

 Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year the deductible goes down 20 percent as long as the customer does not have a loss. Once a loss occurs, the discounted deductible applies and then resets back to the full deductible amount.

 Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state and is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Premiums in South Florida generally run high. Online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

cards.headline: Florida fentanyl summit in Orlando draws teens, grieving parents and DEA chief
cards.teaser: Teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined grieving parents and DEA Administrator Terrance Cole at the Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week to discuss stopping fentanyl deaths.
cards.body:
The Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando drew students from anti-drug coalitions across the country who traveled to Florida to learn about the resurgence of fentanyl. Hannah Kahn, 18, explained what brought her to the summit, saying she has a relative addicted to methamphetamine and seeing how that destroyed his life encouraged her to prevent that from happening to others. Jasmine Figueroa, 19, offered pointed advice for adults on how to talk to young people about drugs, saying it is not a taboo topic and adults should tell them what cocaine is because they're going to get educated one way or another.

 This year's summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a partner. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole spent time with victim families and discussed the ongoing threat, saying the poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels.

 Cole pointed to new tools from the current administration, explaining the president has designated the cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for the DEA to target. Mari Rodriguez's daughter, Imam, died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023 after making the mistake of buying a Percocet pill that had fentanyl in it. Rodriguez said the fight against fentanyl should have started in 2009, when the first fentanyl was found on American streets.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs low-altitude Blue Angels flyover in Pensacola as safety reviews draw scrutiny
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended low-altitude military flyovers after a Navy Blue Angels jet flew so low over a crowded Pensacola beach Wednesday that chairs and tents went
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended low-altitude military flyovers after a Navy Blue Angels jet flew so low over a crowded Pensacola beach Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears. The Navy initially said it was conducting a thorough safety review, but Trump administration officials quickly praised the maneuver instead. Hegseth wrote on his personal X account that "the flyovers will continue until morale improves," while Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell posted "Carry on Patriots" alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above beachgoers' heads. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump administration political appointee, said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. Navy officials would not say if a routine flight debrief was the thorough safety review the service promised the day before. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing beachgoers photographing a Blue Angels jet with the words "Freedom" and "It's okay to love America."

 The incident marks at least the third time Hegseth has voiced support for military maneuvers that drew scrutiny and safety investigations. In March, he ended an Army investigation into helicopters hovering near Kid Rock's Tennessee home, saying "No punishment. Carry on, patriots." Months later, he lifted suspensions of eight South Carolina National Guard helicopter pilots who conducted a low flyover during a July 4 event. In both prior cases, Hegseth's intervention led to the end of safety investigations. Pentagon spokesman Jacob Bliss said he had nothing further to provide when asked if the social media posts meant another investigation had been halted. Aviation safety consultant Jeff Guzzetti, who used to investigate crashes for the National Transportation Safety Board and Federal Aviation Administration, called the behavior reckless and said a cavalier attitude from top military leaders can only lead to accidents. Former Transportation Department Inspector General Mary Schiavo said Blue Angels demonstrations are exceedingly dangerous and not something to be performed over people.

cards.headline: Florida Rep. Fabian Basabe Ordered to Pay $450,000 in Sexual Harassment Case
cards.teaser: A Leon County jury found Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation, ordering him to pay $450,000.
cards.body:
Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe ended the week facing a $450,000 civil judgment after a Leon County jury found him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The case was brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother.

 Basabe represented himself despite having no legal training. The trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders. Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told him that if an attorney had done half of what he had done, they would have been sanctioned.

 Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. After the verdict, however, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake. Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations.

 He has not been criminally charged, and an outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation. Basabe is seeking reelection this fall, and the verdict could also renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action.

hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained, more expected this summer
hero.teaser: Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike, both now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.
hero.body:
Two brush fires broke out in Martin County this week, including one ignited by a lightning strike, and both are now fully contained and under monitoring by the Florida Forest Service. Officials are warning that conditions favorable for brush fires will continue throughout the summer months as the region remains in peak fire season.

 David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them highly receptive when lightning strikes occur. However, he emphasized that residents should not be alarmed by these conditions, as they are typical for this time of year. Grubitch explained that while rain often extinguishes fires immediately after they start, some fires can travel underground and resurface days later, making them more difficult to detect and contain.

 The Florida Forest Service is relying on public assistance to help monitor and respond to brush fires quickly. Grubitch stressed that residents play a crucial role in helping the department do its job effectively and urged people to never assume someone else has already reported a brush fire they spot. He emphasized the importance of immediate notification, saying that if residents see something, they should say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control. Quick reporting remains one of the most effective tools in preventing small fires from becoming larger, more dangerous blazes that threaten homes and natural areas.

 With summer conditions expected to continue creating favorable environments for brush fires, the Florida Forest Service will maintain its heightened monitoring and response efforts throughout the season. The department continues to track contained fires and remains prepared to respond to new incidents as they arise. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any signs of smoke or fire to local authorities immediately, regardless of whether they believe others may have already called it in. Officials stress that multiple reports of the same fire are preferable to a fire going unreported and potentially spreading out of control.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: Dave and Faren Motz of Hobe Sound are asking for community support as Dave battles head and neck cancer, facing nearly $20,000 in out-of-pocket costs for treatment.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis. Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren homeschooled all three of their children, and the family started a farm where they served children. Years later, the couple moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer.

 As the couple searched for healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource. Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket.

 Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid. Dave, a former firefighter who had long been the family's provider, now has an 85% chance of recovery according to doctors. Faren now works to support them both at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show support can visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County man leads Martin County deputies on 100 mph chase through Indiantown
cards.teaser: Markell Tillman, 33, drove more than 100 mph on State Road 710 before leading deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown and onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City.
cards.body:
A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710, one of the area's most dangerous roads. Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled. Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly.

 Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95. Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody.

 Tillman was arrested on charges including fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offering free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.

 The program offers one alarm per household and has no income or priority group requirements, making it available to any qualifying resident regardless of financial status. The alarms are available while supplies last on a first-come, first-served basis, so interested residents should act promptly to secure one. Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out an online survey to determine their eligibility for the program. For more information about the free pool alarm program, residents can call (772) 462-3501.

 According to the coalition, a pool alarm serves as one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning. The program emphasizes that pool alarms are not a standalone safety solution but rather part of a comprehensive approach to water safety. Residents should note that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm, but the battery is not included with the free alarm.

 The initiative aims to increase water safety awareness and provide practical tools to help prevent drowning incidents in residential pools throughout Martin County. By distributing these alarms at no cost, the program seeks to remove financial barriers that might otherwise prevent families from implementing additional safety measures around their pools. The combination of free access and the comprehensive safety messaging demonstrates the coalition's commitment to protecting children and preventing water-related accidents in the community.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project
cards.body:
Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized.

 The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

 Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said the school was already scheduled for significant construction before the hurricane struck. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Gernaine.

 "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on." The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Residents Report Five Cyclospora Cases Since May
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health has confirmed five cases of cyclospora in the Treasure Coast region since May amid nationwide produce contamination outbreaks.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County. The cases are part of nationwide outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora linked to contaminated produce, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, causing many South Florida residents to change their eating habits and avoid leafy greens altogether.

 Families across the region are steering clear of salads and contaminated produce that can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are avoiding lettuce and similar foods. Jenny Rhodes said she misses her salads and berries but believes it is better to be careful.

 In West Palm Beach, George Lorenz said he has heard about the outbreak and is staying away from affected produce. In Boynton Beach, shopper Hendriette Peckens said she bought oranges, apples and bread instead of greens and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

 Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said the outbreaks are not an excuse to abandon healthy eating. She recommended consumers focus on produce with protective outer layers, suggesting they stick to melon and foods with harder skin that can be peeled, including bananas, melons and avocados. However, she warned that people still need to wash these items before cutting into them and peeling them. Barone also said beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein.

 Barone's biggest warning was to avoid bagged lettuce if possible. She recommended buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. She also warned that berries, especially raspberries, are difficult to clean properly and should be avoided.

 Barone recommended cleaning produce using a 1 to 3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water. Consumers should soak, massage and clean off produce and make sure to cook vegetables. She emphasized that washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them is essential, and consumers should wash items with harder skins before cutting into them.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrests nephew in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes
hero.teaser: Dale A. Mincey, 41, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with the death of his uncle, 66-year-old Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes.
hero.body:
Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with Barnes' death. Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. Deputies said the fatal shooting was premeditated.

 Karen Moye, who lived in the home with Mincey and Barnes, was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police, an arrest affidavit said. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said during a press conference Tuesday that detectives uncovered information indicating Moye, the victim's sister and mother of the suspect, knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to the homicide investigation. She has been charged with false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. He leaves behind three adult children.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
cards.body:
Concerns over contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks are prompting South Florida residents to reconsider their food choices, with some avoiding leafy greens entirely. The outbreaks have affected thousands nationwide and include lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials have confirmed local cases stretching from the Palm Beaches to the Treasure Coast, including two cases in St. Lucie County.

 The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May. Two cases were reported in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The contamination concerns have led families across the region to change their eating habits at restaurants, grocery stores, and fast-food chains.

 Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, who were visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Other families are similarly steering clear of leafy greens altogether as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country. The widespread nature of the outbreaks has left many consumers uncertain about which products are safe to purchase and consume.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, offered guidance for consumers looking to maintain healthy diets while avoiding potentially contaminated produce. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She advises consumers to focus on produce with protective outer layers and to wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them.

 For those seeking alternatives to leafy greens, Barone suggests that beans and nuts are safe options that still provide fiber and protein. She specifically recommends cleaning produce using a mixture of one part distilled white vinegar to three parts water. The outbreaks have highlighted the importance of proper food handling and preparation practices for consumers across South Florida.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce neighbors pack planning meeting over Causeway Cove high-rise development proposal
cards.teaser: The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall.
cards.body:
The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space.

 The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing.

 Neighbors packed the chamber during the Monday meeting. Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic, saying nobody has thought this out and predicting massive traffic jams with nobody able to get on or off the island.

 City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved, stating the city does not have a play here and this is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step in the process.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie couple fights rezoning of lot behind home near Crosstown Parkway
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie couple is searching for answers after the city council voted to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial.
cards.body:
Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo have called Port St. Lucie home since purchasing their property, drawn by what Margaret described as the beautiful setting and backyard views of nature. In a unanimous vote, the Port St.

 Lucie City Council approved rezoning the lot behind their yard, where trees currently stand, from residential to commercial. One council member said the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood, explaining that adding commercial closer to neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, which reduces overall traffic because shorter trips reduce the burden on the overall network.

 The Mucciolos fought the rezoning for months and feel their voices have gone unheard. The council held its second reading Monday. While there was public comment, it was what is called a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges, applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion.

 The Mucciolos say the process needs to change to be logical, transparent, caring, and provide hope for people. They say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one. Joseph Mucciolo said he believes in six months or a year, the trees behind their home will be gone.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents return home after nearly 2 years following structural damage repairs
cards.teaser: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos.
cards.body:
Residents told WPTV they were notified last month they could return to their condos, after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. Katie Johnson was the first to share to WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return.

 WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, saying they're still moving the dirt back under the buildings.

 Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot. Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia.

 Eric Johnson said the financial toll has been severe and that he and his family had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors, like Eric Johnson, who cannot return and feels so bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement after 1,162 stops in four weeks
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies to target speeding and reckless driving on Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break.

 He is also placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern. Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive.

 Benning said the county sees a lot of excessive speeding, noting that someone recently passed her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues described stops on those same roads, including a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road, another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1, and a top speed of 73 mph on Indian River Drive, where the limit is 25 mph.

 In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

hero.headline: Indian River County families can apply for free or reduced-price student meals starting July 15
hero.teaser: Families in Indian River County are able to apply for free or reduced price meals for students starting July 15.
hero.body:
Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15 through the district's online portal. While six schools in the county will automatically provide free meals to all students during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs, other families may still qualify based on household size and income levels.

 The application process begins at www.LINQConnect.com, where parents must either sign in to an existing account or create a new one. After logging in, families should search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach and add their student to the application using the Student ID number and the child's formal name as it appears in FOCUS, the district's student information system. The application can be accessed from the website homepage by clicking School Services at the top menu and then selecting Free and Reduced Meal Application.

 District officials are encouraging families to submit one application per household to determine eligibility. The application requires families to provide information about household size and income to determine eligibility for the federal nutrition programs. By submitting a single application for all children in the household, families can streamline the process and find out if they qualify for free meals, reduced-price meals, or neither option. The program is designed to ensure that students have access to nutritious meals during the school day regardless of their family's financial situation.

 Families who have questions about the meal programs or need assistance with the application process can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director. O'Keefe can be reached by phone at (772) 564-5041 or by email at shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org. District officials recommend that families apply as early as possible to ensure their eligibility status is determined before the start of the 2026-2027 school year.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low ridership

cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. Dambeck said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates, noting that air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand.

 Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if the airline had hung in there. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is easy and close.

 Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said Boston is seeing great demand. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

 Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning, as JetBlue will evaluate continuously. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

cards.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian as severe weather strikes Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather battered the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to th
cards.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather battered the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom captured the waterspout moving through the area.

 The severe weather stretched across the region, bringing heavy rain and significant lightning activity. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotters recorded video of heavy rain moving through the area.

 Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said.

 Lightning strikes caused fires in Port St. Lucie. Lucie County Fire District crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot.

 Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening. Radar picked up significant lightning in the area at the time, though Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

 The severe weather extended to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Moore O'Rourke summarized what many across the region felt as the storms moved through. "I mean it was radical.

 I mean it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather reminded residents of nature's unpredictable power.
